newsitem.title: PERU: Peru to buy $100 million in July for foreign debt.
newsitem.headline: Peru to buy $100 million in July for foreign debt.

text.p: The Peruvian government is planning to purchase up to $100 million in July to meet foreign debt payments, banking sources said Tuesday.
The sources, who did not want to be named, said the purchase would be made by state-owned Banco de La Nacion from the Peruvian Central Reserve Bank.
The Central Bank has said that during the first half of the year, the government bought $441 million destined to service foreign debt.
Economy Minister Jorge Camet said in April that Peru would pay off $1.38 billion of its external debt in 1997.
Total private and public external debt of Peru was $27.436 billion in March, down from $33.513 billion in December, thanks to a Brady-style plan that restructured debt to commercial banks.
